# Success

<!--
Projects should have a definition of done that is measurable, and a
thorough understanding going in of what the risks are to delivery
-->

## Definition of done
<!--
What does success look like?
-->

The project is complete when:

- the package is published on CRAN and installs or locates Vale on Linux, macOS and Windows
- it lints R code comments, vignettes and READMEs using a default style that ships with the package, with rules configurable from a file at the package root
- the style is also published so that it can be installed and used directly by Vale users
- the defaults have been tuned so that the tool runs without error on the 100 most downloaded CRAN packages
- the GitHub Action, pre-commit hook and AGENTS.md command are released and documented

## Measuring success
<!--
How will we know when success is achieved, what markers can we use
along the way
-->

During the project, progress is tracked by milestone completion against the dates in the project plan, with work visible in public GitHub issues.
After release, the main indicators are the number of packages using the GitHub Action, found via GitHub code search, and rules or vocabulary contributed by people outside the project.
Completion of the grant does not depend on adoption, since uptake of developer tooling takes longer than the grant period.

## Future work
<!--
How could this be extended / developed in the future by yourself
and/or the community in general?
-->

- Roxygen-aware linting, so that rules can be applied per help topic and example code is not treated as prose
- Linting of error and warning messages
- Additional named styles, so that organisations with a house style can publish their own rule sets for R packages
